verdict.rationale: Databricks shows agent-oriented governance building blocks — Unity Catalog enforces access control, lineage, and auditing on every data/AI interaction (docs-19, docs-38), and the MCP tooling docs mention giving 'your agent governed access to third-party and SaaS tools' (docs-31) with discovery/authentication flows for MCP servers (docs-50). However, none of this evidence specifically documents an API credential-issuance mechanism (e.g., scoped service-principal tokens or OAuth scopes) purpose-built for handing an agent least-privilege access; it's inferred from general Unity Catalog governance and MCP 'governed access' language rather than a dedicated credential-scoping feature description. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of scoped/least-privilege credential or token issuance workflow for agents, and any hands-on/independent confirmation that such scoping works as intended.
